extracted.intended_audience: ERC peer reviewers: Panel Chairs, Panel Members, Panel Evaluators and Remote Referees for ERC Starting and Consolidator Grant calls
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation rules for peer reviewers assessing ERC Starting and Consolidator Grant proposals (two-step evaluation including remote reviews, panel meetings and interviews). Covers what to evaluate, scoring, conflicts of interest, reviewer conduct and panel deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence as the sole evaluation criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific excellence is the sole criterion of evaluation and is at the core of the peer review evaluation process. It is applied to both the Research Project and the Principal Investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No other criteria than the evaluation elements defined in the ERC Work Programme must be considered. Societal impact is not an ERC evaluation criterion. Incorrect application or use of irrelevant criteria is a procedural error and may justify re-evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project — Ground‑breaking nature, ambition and potential impact
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent does the proposed research address important challenges? To what extent are the objectives ambitious and beyond the state of the art (e.g. novel concepts and approaches or development between or across disciplines)? To what extent is the proposed research high risk-high gain?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the project is genuinely ground‑breaking and ambitious; consider novelty across or between disciplines and whether potential payoff justifies risk. Use the extended synopsis (Part B1) at step 1 and the full proposal at step 2 to judge these elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project — Scientific approach, feasibility and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent is the outlined scientific approach feasible bearing in mind the extent that the proposed research is high risk/high gain? To what extent are the proposed research methodology and working arrangements appropriate to achieve the goals of the project? To what extent does the proposal involve the development of novel methodology? To what extent are the proposed timescales, resources and PI commitment adequate and properly justified?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At step 1 assess feasibility (based on Extended Synopsis). At step 2 evaluate methodology, timescales, resource justification and PI time commitment (based on full Scientific Proposal and budget). Consider whether risk is identified and managed; novel methodology should be evidenced and justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator — Intellectual capacity, creativity and track record
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent has the PI demonstrated the ability to conduct ground‑breaking research? To what extent does the PI provide evidence of creative independent thinking? To what extent does the PI have the required scientific expertise and capacity to successfully execute the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess PI's independence, creativity and evidence of leadership/academic excellence. Consider publications (including properly referenced preprints), scientific contributions and suitability to lead the proposed high‑risk research. Focus on scientific content rather than journal impact factors (ERC follows DORA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 1 scope and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: At step 1, Panel Members acting as generalists review Part B1 only (extended synopsis together with PI’s track record and CV) and assess feasibility and PI track record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel Members should provide individual remote reviews for assigned proposals at step 1, suggest possible Remote Referees for step 2, and avoid budget recommendations at step 1. Step 1 panel scores are A (pass to step 2), B (high quality but not pass), C (not sufficient).

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2 scope and requirements (including interviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: At step 2, Panel Members and Remote Referees review the complete retained proposals (Parts B1 and B2), the resources (including the budget table) and time commitment extracted from Part A; interviews with applicants take place and are taken into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate detailed methodology, timescales, resources and budget justification at step 2. Panels may recommend budget reductions where expenses (excluding salary costs) are not fully justified; any budget recommendations must be documented and explained in panel comments. Interview performance contributes to the assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring system: numerical marks and panel grades
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual numerical marks range from 1 (non-competitive) to 5 (exceptional), in integers or halves; Remote Referees provide a qualitative three‑option recommendation (highly recommended, recommended, not recommended). Panel final scores are A, B or C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the full range of the mark scale where appropriate; ensure numerical marks are consistent with written comments. Numerical marks are inputs to panel deliberations and are not communicated to applicants. Panel labels: Score A = proposal sufficient to pass to step 2 / recommended for funding if fully meets excellence (step 2); Score B = high quality but not pass / meets some but not all aspects; Score C = not sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual review content and required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: During the individual remote review, reviewers evaluate and mark the proposals according to (1) Research Project — provide a succinct explanatory comment; (2) Principal Investigator — indicate extent of agreement with statements related to PI and optionally provide explanatory comment; and award marks for both elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver concise but substantial individual reviews by the deadlines. Reviews are reproduced in Evaluation Reports sent to applicants, so be clear, factual and constructive. Avoid ambiguity about what element is being commented on and ensure comments align with the marks given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality standards and conduct for reviewers' comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual reviews should be genuine, succinct but substantial, impeccably polite, and form statements with explanations of key strengths and weaknesses in light of the evaluation criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must: provide substantial explanatory comments (not mere summaries); use dispassionate, analytical and unambiguous language; write grammatically correct, clear sentences with no jargon; make critical comments constructive; ensure comments align with marks; avoid self-declared insufficient expertise; avoid references to applicant age, nationality, gender or personal matters; avoid dismissive language about applicant, science or field; be aware of unconscious bias and not penalise non‑conventional career paths; avoid comments on Host Institution standing; do not consider societal impact; avoid direct comparison with other proposals or prior assessments; avoid copy‑paste; avoid comments on ethical/security aspects (handled separately by ERCEA); avoid budget recommendations at step 1 and salary recommendations; provide justification if recommending budget cuts at step 2; consider Covid‑19 impacts on CVs where indicated; focus on scientific content, not Journal Impact Factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest and confidentiality rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers should not be in situations where impartiality may be questioned. A list of conflicts is displayed in the online system and experts must confirm absence of conflict when accepting and when submitting reviews. Confidentiality is contractual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of conflicts: I am PI or team member in the proposal; I was involved in preparation; I'd benefit directly if proposal accepted/rejected; employed/contracted by host or partner institution in past 3 years; involved in management of host/partner in past 3 years; collaborating scientifically with PI in past 5 years; mentor/mentee relationship; family ties or close personal relationship; scientific rivalry/hostility; National Contact Point or Enterprise Europe Network; member of a programme committee; any other situation precluding impartiality. Experts must declare conflicts; Panel Chair should avoid assigning conflicted reviewers. Breach of confidentiality or Code of Conduct can lead to contract termination. No contact with applicants/hosts about the evaluation during or after the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and responsibilities of Panel Chairs, Panel Members and Lead Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel Chairs and Panel Members must familiarise with proposals, perform individual remote reviews, participate in panel meetings, and deliver concise and substantial reviews. Panels may assign a Lead Reviewer responsible for introducing the proposal and drafting the panel comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel Chairs additionally chair meetings, attend initial and final Panel Chairs' meetings, (re)allocate proposals to panels, assign proposals to reviewers (paying attention to conflicts), ensure panels produce required deliverables and select experts for remote evaluation. Panel Members are expected to be available for both panel meetings and to reflect openness to inter-/multi-disciplinary perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remote Referees: role, selection and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Remote Referees are external specialists providing specialised expertise, typically 2–5 per proposal; they deliver individual assessments remotely and do not participate in panel meetings. They are usually non-paid and mainly involved at step 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remote Referees are nominated by reviewers/panels and approved/selected by Panel Chairs; any researcher worldwide may be nominated subject to accreditation and conflict checks. Their qualitative recommendation (highly recommended / recommended / not recommended) and reviews feed into panel deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel comment: purpose and required content
rubrics_metrics.description: The panel comment is the key element provided to applicants and should clearly explain the reason(s), respecting the ERC evaluation criterion, which make the proposal succeed or fail. It is a conclusive comment approved by the panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel comments must reflect main points from individual reviews, panel discussion and (at step 2) the interview. They should document important weaknesses revealed by discussion, distinguish scientific recommendations from budget recommendations (the latter are binding to ERCEA) and explain any panel budget recommendations. Panel comments are part of the Evaluation Report sent to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliverables of panel meetings include: (1) Ranked list of proposals; (2) Panel comments approved by the panel; (3) List of approved Remote Referees (only at step 1); (4) Panel report; (5) Panel Recommendations to the ERC Scientific Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels must ensure all required documents are produced with required quality standards by the end of the panel meetings. The Evaluation Report for each proposal contains the Panel recommendation (A/B/C and ranking range), panel comment and individual reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget review and justification at step 2
rubrics_metrics.description: At step 2, the panel analyses the budget, its justification and the requested contribution. Recommendations for reduction may be made if some expenses (excluding salary costs) are not considered fully justified. Cuts across-the-board are not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any budget reduction recommendations must be documented and explained in the panel comments for each concerned proposal, based on analysis of resources requested and necessary to carry out the work. Salary recommendations should be avoided because they depend on national/institutional rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility and eligibility: detection and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Admissibility and eligibility assessment is carried out by ERCEA; however, if an expert considers a proposal potentially inadmissible or ineligible during evaluation, they should report it immediately to ERCEA Scientific Officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In rare cases proposals can be declared inadmissible/ineligible during or after peer review if non‑compliance is confirmed. Experts should not make final admissibility decisions themselves but report concerns promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of interdisciplinary proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Interdisciplinary proposals are encouraged. The initial applicant choice of panel is paramount, but proposals flagged as cross-panel/cross-domain may receive additional reviews from other panels. Applicants may indicate a second panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels must ensure cross-panel proposals receive equal and fair treatment, request appropriate additional expertise when necessary, and may reallocate proposals to other panels with agreement of both Panel Chairs to ensure competent evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and interactions during remote review
rubrics_metrics.description: During the individual remote review process there shall be no discussions of the proposals between reviewers, and Panel Members should not disclose assigned proposals to other experts before panel meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a Panel Member has insufficient expertise for an assigned proposal, they must inform ERCEA Scientific Officers and the Panel Chair immediately so reassignment can occur. Maintain strict confidentiality of proposal content until allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion requests by applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may request that up to three specific persons not act as peer reviewers for their proposal; such requests are made at submission time and treated confidentially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluded persons (if independent experts participating in evaluation) may be excluded as long as ERCEA can still have the proposal evaluated by qualified experts. If the excluded person is a Panel Member they will be informed confidentially of the request. Exclusion of a Panel Chair may trigger consultation with the Deputy Panel Chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking methodology and use of voting
rubrics_metrics.description: Panels may use successive elimination stages, random or neutral discussion order, and, while consensus is preferred, may use a voting system (e.g. majority vote) to expedite ranking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each Panel Member has one vote per proposal considered; any member under a conflict of interest cannot be involved in discussion nor vote for that proposal. Panels should document ranking decisions and ensure fairness and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency and preparation expectations for panel meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel Members are expected to familiarise with all proposals in the panel and to assess a subset in detail in preparation for panel meetings; before step 2 they should prepare for interviews by identifying strengths, weaknesses and concerns raised in individual reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good preparation increases meeting efficiency; Panel Members should read briefing documents (including webcast briefings) and deliver concise and substantive input. At step 1 propose suitable Remote Referees for step 2 specialist assessment.
